name: Vai Script
notes: Created by Momolu Duwalu Bukele in Liberia, c. 1832-1834; the missionary-recorded "dream" founding narrative is internally inconsistent across near-contemporary transcriptions and is treated by scholars as a likely religious/status-conferring gloss on a mundane contact-inspired invention process. Vai characters bear no visual resemblance to Cherokee ones despite a documented possible indirect Cherokee contact channel (Austin Curtis, a Cherokee man who married into a Vai chief's family in 1823) — supporting transmission of the concept of syllabic writing rather than sign-copying. Still in active use — `latest: null`.
